# MDL012 mdl-deprecated-name

A reference uses a `renamed_from` name, or a source uses a pre-cycle-1 spelling that the parser still reads.

## What it does

Edit the reference to the new name. The clause itself is reported once no lock entry needs it (that half needs the lock and is evaluated by the binary).

### Bridged pre-cycle-1 spellings

Each spelling below is read as its replacement and reported as MDL012 (warn) naming the replacement (grmb-spec 11.1, D168). The list is closed.

- `include "p";` for `use "p";`
- `evidence tests SEL;` and `evidence ref "S";` for `verified_by`
- a `kind test` vmodel for `verified_by SEL;` on the `verifies` target (drop `level`)
- `review=` for `until=` on `assumed`
- `step S -> { .. }` for `step S : { .. }`
- an arm `p -> c` for `p => c`
- `title "t";` for a `///` line
- `requires page P;` for `on page P;`
- an actor `node N;` for `in node N;`
- `verified_by` on a `system` (it is ignored)
- `goal P as K { }` for `goal P { attr dimension = K; }`

The chain hops `->`, `via FLOW` and `outcome { v <- S; }` are not bridged: they are MDL000.

## Why it matters

A `renamed_from` name keeps old locks and references alive across a rename. A reference that still uses it will break the day the clause goes.

## Remedy

Edit the reference to the new name.

## Examples

### Fires case 1

```grmb expect=fire file=design/model.grmb
grimble = "2";
module m;
node new_name : trusted {
  renamed_from old_name;
  alias legacy;
}
flow f : old_name -> legacy {
  label Public;
}
```
